t:
(a) In General.—Chapter 17 of title 14, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:
“§ 678. Aircraft accident investigations“(a) In General.—Whenever the Commandant of the Coast Guard conducts an accident investigation of an accident involving an aircraft under the jurisdiction of the Commandant, the records and report of the investigation shall be treated in accordance with this section.“(b) Public Disclosure of Certain Accident Investigation Information.—“(1) In general.—Subject to paragraph (2), the Commandant, upon request, shall publicly disclose unclassified tapes, scientific reports, and other factual information pertinent to an aircraft accident investigation.“(2) Conditions.—The Commandant shall only disclose information requested pursuant to paragraph (1) if the Commandant determines—“(A) that such tapes, reports, or other information would be included within and releasable with the final accident investigation report; and“(B) that release of such tapes, reports, or other information—“(i) would not undermine the ability of accident or safety investigators to continue to conduct the investigation; and“(ii) would not compromise national security.“(3) Restriction.—A disclosure under paragraph (1) may not be made by or through officials with responsibility for, or who are conducting, a safety investigation with respect to the accident.“(c) Opinions Regarding Causation of Accident.—Following an aircraft accident referred to in subsection (a)—“(1) if the evidence surrounding the accident is sufficient for the investigators who conduct the accident investigation to come to an opinion as to the cause or causes of the accident, the final report of the accident investigation shall set forth the opinion of the investigators as to the cause or causes of the accident; and“(2) if the evidence surrounding the accident is not sufficient for the investigators to come to an opinion as to the cause or causes of the accident, the final report of the accident investigation shall include a description of those factors, if any, that, in the opinion of the investigators, substantially contributed to or caused the accident.“(d) Use of Information in Civil or Criminal Proceedings.—For purposes of any civil or criminal proceeding arising from an aircraft accident referred to in subsection (a), any opinion of the accident investigators as to the cause of, or the factors contributing to, the accident set forth in the accident investigation report may not be considered as evidence in such proceeding, nor may such report be considered an admission of liability by the United States or by any person referred to in such report.“(e) Definitions.—For purposes of this section—“(1) the term ‘accident investigation’ means any form of investigation by Coast Guard personnel of an aircraft accident referred to in subsection (a), other than a safety investigation; and“(2) the term ‘safety investigation’ means an investigation by Coast Guard personnel of an aircraft accident referred to 
in subsection (a) that is conducted solely to determine the cause of the accident and to obtain information that may prevent the occurrence of similar accidents.”
. 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The analysis for chapter 17 of title 14, United States Code, as amended by this Act, is further amended by adding at the end the following:


“678. 
Aircraft accident investigations.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that public disclosure "upon request" brings outsiders into the process. But releasing information to the public is one-way transparency, not consultation or coordination with outside parties before a federal decision. The investigations are conducted entirely by Coast Guard personnel, and the section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. The provision on civil or criminal proceedings only limits the evidentiary use of investigators' opinions.
fable.s: the Commandant, upon request, shall publicly disclose unclassified tapes, scientific reports, and other factual information pertinent to an aircraft accident investigation

opus.w: This section sets rules for Coast Guard aircraft accident investigations, which Coast Guard personnel carry out, and for when their results may be released. Releasing information on request is one-way disclosure. It doesn't involve outsiders in any federal decision through a comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation. The civil-proceedings clause restricts how investigators' opinions can be used as evidence. It doesn't grant an outside party a right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: the Commandant, upon request, shall publicly disclose unclassified tapes, scientific reports, and other factual information pertinent to an aircraft accident investigation.
opus.b:
1. **The tempting wrong reading:** Under subsection (b), the Commandant must publicly disclose investigation materials "upon request," and subsection (d) mentions civil and criminal proceedings. Both could look like outsiders taking part. Neither one fits the definition:
   - A disclosure request is just the public getting information. Members of the public don't advise on, comment on, or object to any Coast Guard decision.
   - Subsection (d) limits what can be used as evidence in lawsuits. It doesn't give anyone a right to sue over a federal decision.
   - The investigation itself is run entirely by Coast Guard personnel.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates the public disclosure of information regarding aircraft accident investigations. While it involves the public, it does not require consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties before the government makes a decision. The disclosure happens after the investigation is conducted, and there is no advisory board, comment period, or hearing described that would allow outsiders to influence the investigation or its findings. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Public Disclosure of Certain Accident Investigation Information.—“(1) In general.—Subject to paragraph (2), the Commandant, upon request, shall publicly disclose unclassified tapes, scientific reports, and other factual information pertinent to an aircraft accident investigation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement to "publicly disclose" information constitutes participation because it involves the general public. However, the definition of participation requires consultation or coordination *before* a decision is made, or an advisory role in the decision-making process. Mere disclosure of information after an investigation is complete is transparency, not participation in the decision-making process itself. There is no mechanism here for the public to comment on, advise, or influence the investigation or the final report before it is issued.
